clue.text: Dating an old tennis champion's cool

parts.note: Margaret Court, the Australian who won a record 24 Grand Slam singles titles, plus the possessive S
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A former tennis star is said to be playing it cool about a new romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Court is a retired Australian tennis great; her name plus the possessive 's gives the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing someone with a view to marriage is what dating once meant, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: See way out of folly that's greed

indicators.note: C goes in and the way comes out of the word for folly

parts.note: stupidity is folly
ST is short for street, a way
the letter C sounds like 'see'

explanation.surface: Someone spots an escape from foolishness that turns out to be avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' swaps ST for C in STUPIDITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice for money or possessions: the word comes from the Roman god of desire.

clue.text: You sell feminist underwear, bottoms only, leading to end of bra? That's radical

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of each word is its last letter
end of the word takes just its final letter

explanation.surface: A shop sells feminist lingerie, briefs only, so no bra: an extreme idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottoms only' takes the last letters of 'You sell feminist underwear'; 'end of' adds the last letter of bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme in opinion: the word is a prefix and noun for someone holding extreme views.

clue.text: An obsession, perhaps, with something found on the French Riviera?

definitions.text: something found on the French Riviera

parts.note: an obsession is 'a thing', which is what remains of the word for swimming once its top letter is taken off

explanation.surface: Is a fixation with Riviera beaches what drives people there?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: remove the first letter of BATHING and you get A THING, a slangy word for an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without a swimsuit top is a familiar sight on beaches of the Côte d'Azur, such as Saint-Tropez.

clue.text: Like some trousers to appear hot on high priest

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next part

parts.note: H stands for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: high here means intoxicated, so the letters stagger about

explanation.surface: A priest appears in hot, tight trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' means drunk, so the priest staggers into a new order; 'on' in a down clue puts the hot letter on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers cut to sit low on the waist are described with this word, which names the body part they rest on.

clue.text: Experts backing spies' routine

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the agency letters are reversed

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Professionals support the everyday work of secret agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and dull: something humdrum and everyday is lacking poetry or flair.

clue.text: Neighbour displaying a 26 after sun comes out

indicators.note: the sun's letter leaving the word is signalled by 'comes out', as when something is removed from a container

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, the puzzle's theme word, a word for a woman's bosom

explanation.surface: Someone next door is seen sunbathing topless once the sun appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out' looks like the sun emerging, but it tells us to take the sun's letter out of the theme word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to neighbour something is to lie right next to it, to border or adjoin it.

clue.text: A meal best canned in tin, say

indicators.note: canned can mean wrecked or junked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The finest meal you can have is one packed in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' looks like it describes the meal but rearranges 'A meal best'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a common non-precious metal, an example of this class as opposed to gold or silver.

clue.text: Gift books coming under 'Fiction'

indicators.note: in a down clue, the books are placed below the fiction

parts.note: a tale is a story, a fiction
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A present of novels filed under the fiction section.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a common crossword way to clue books.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is a gift, and the word comes from a parable about coins.

clue.text: Was unsure about European wearing the French underwear as outer garments sometimes

indicators.note: the doubting goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: to doubt is to be unsure
le is French for 'the'

indicators.note: the European is wearing the underwear, so it goes inside

parts.note: bras are underwear

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over a European in French lingerie worn as outerwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the European sits inside the French lingerie, and that whole lot sits inside the doubting.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackets and coats are often cut with overlapping front panels and two rows of buttons, a style described by this term.

clue.text: Accommodate going back and forth

definitions.note: to accommodate a guest is to give them a bed, and the phrase is the setter's own word used as the definition and the palindrome alike

indicators.note: the letters read the same in both directions, so the word works going back as well as forth

parts.note: to accommodate a guest is to give them a bed, and the phrase is the setter's own word used as the definition and the palindrome alike

explanation.surface: Hosting someone involves a lot of to-ing and fro-ing.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the answer itself: it reads identically from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a bed for the night is to lodge or house them, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Roman official for and against Muslim ruler having no function

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the ruler having no function means those letters are taken away from his title

parts.note: a sultan is a Muslim sovereign
tan is short for tangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A debate on a powerless sultan, with arguments on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: TAN, the tangent, is a mathematical function; take it from SULTAN to leave SUL.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a governor of a province acting with a consul's authority held this title.

clue.text: Potentially the cause of most damage inside a restaurant

definitions.text: Potentially the cause of most damage

indicators.note: the word 'inside' is split: its first two letters say look within what follows

parts.note: the rest of 'inside' joins 'a restaurant' as the run of text the letters are taken from

explanation.surface: Which dish on a restaurant menu might do the worst harm?
explanation.walkthrough: Lift and separate: 'in' is the signal, and the letters are drawn from 'side a restaurant'. 'Damage' is slang for the bill, as in 'What's the damage?'
explanation.definitionFit: The priciest item is the one that costs most, and 'damage' is colloquial for the cost of something.

clue.text: White male husband, regularly drunk

indicators.note: a drunk is reeling and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up
taking every other letter of husband, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A white man's husband gets drunk now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes U, B and N from husband; 'drunk' mixes them with MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear part of an egg that turns opaque when cooked is called the white.

clue.text: 'X' on map might show whereabouts of this diabolical theatre's curse

definitions.text: 'X' on map might show whereabouts of this

indicators.note: something diabolical is a terrible mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pirate map marks the spot, while a theatre labours under a dreadful curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diabolical' rearranges the letters of 'theatre's curse'. In the theme, the answer is also slang for an ample bosom.
explanation.definitionFit: On a pirate's map the X marks where the buried hoard of gold and jewels lies.

clue.text: Show up with energy Mars Bars produced

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: produced means made or worked into new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chocolate bars provide energy, a staple of marketing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges MARSBARS to follow E. Mars Bars are a chocolate bar popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to make them feel awkward or ashamed in public.

clue.text: Extremely large number upset by a new dealer in Cheddar?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: a myriad is a countless number

explanation.surface: A cheese trader is shaken by a huge new figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses MYRIAD to DAIRYM. Cheddar, a village in Somerset, gives its name to the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells milk, butter and cheese like Cheddar trades in dairy produce.

clue.text: Live with a friend: British female one's put up at the seaside

definitions.text: one's put up at the seaside

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
a chum is a friend
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone moves in with a pal, while a British woman is being housed by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A large parasol is opened on the sand to give shade on a beach holiday.

clue.text: Unlucky, like chap that's caught short

indicators.note: that's here means the chap that has had its letter taken, read with 'short' as 'chap less C'

parts.note: chap is short of caught, its C, so it is chap less C
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
short of something means less of it

explanation.surface: A man caught short is having bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the answer as 'chap less C': 'caught short' means short of C, cricket's caught, and 'less' is the word for that shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-fated or unfortunate: the word derives from 'hap', an old word for luck.

clue.text: Jaw about everyone before nine in the morning

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the sequence is reversed

parts.note: all means everyone
IX is nine in Roman numerals
AM stands for ante meridiem, morning

explanation.surface: A sore jaw affects everybody before nine o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ALL IX AM to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper jawbone in vertebrates carries this anatomical name.

clue.text: Bad smell around a wee stunted tree

indicators.note: the odour goes around the letter A

parts.note: BO is body odour

indicators.note: stunted means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: wee means tiny, baby-sized

explanation.surface: A tiny stunted tree gives off a bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunted' cuts BABY to BAB.
explanation.definitionFit: An African species with a massively swollen trunk is a famous example.

clue.text: Around one hour in Paris? Sadly, it could fly by

indicators.note: the reversed pair is placed within the jumbled city letters
sadly, as in badly, says the letters of the city go awry
around means turned about, so one and hour are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller spends an unhappy hour in Paris, watching something float overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' reverses I and H to make HI, which goes 'in' AIRSP, the anagram of PARIS signalled by 'Sadly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible is a powered lighter-than-air craft that could drift past overhead.

clue.text: Special quality that's needed by female member of cast

parts.note: X means 'by' as in measurements like 3 x 4
an actor is one of a play's cast

explanation.surface: A woman in a play must have that indefinable something.
explanation.walkthrough: X is read as 'by' in dimensions such as 'six by four'.
explanation.definitionFit: That indefinable star quality, named after a TV talent show, is a special gift that sets someone apart.

clue.text: Roots supply trunk

indicators.note: supply is read as 'supplely', bending the letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: Roots feed water to the tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb of supple: flexibly, so the letters bend.
explanation.definitionFit: The human trunk is the body without the head and limbs.

clue.text: One holding 26 in small room shows some intellectual capability

parts.note: 26 across is the theme word for a bosom, and the garment that supports it is a bra
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A bra in a cramped room proves somebody has a few brains.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a unit of the brain, so having one suggests at least a little mental capacity.

clue.text: Cut thread … half of which lost by hesitating?

indicators.note: half of which is kept and the other half lost, so only the first three letters of the thread survive

parts.note: 'which' points back to the thread in the definition, and 'lost' says the rest of it has gone, leaving only half
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A cut thread loses half its length because someone dithered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of which lost' drops EAD from THREAD; 'which' stands for the thread named in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In weaving, the loose end left when a warp is cut off is called by this word: a loose fringe or tuft.

clue.text: Journalist thrown by boy band not working

indicators.note: the editor is thrown out, ejected, by the band, so those letters go

parts.note: Busted is a British boy band from the 2000s
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter gets ejected by a pop group that has stopped performing.
explanation.walkthrough: Busted were a British pop-punk boy band; take away ED (editor) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken or kaput: something that is no longer functioning is said to have gone this way.

clue.text: Withdraw from sun, with its required effect now lost on 26, largely

parts.note: what a sunbather wants from the sun is a tan
26 across is a bosom; a large one takes a DD cup size

indicators.note: lost here means astray, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from the sun, its desired effect undone on their chest.
explanation.walkthrough: A large bosom takes a DD bra cup, hence '26, largely'; 'lost' jumbles 'now'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a position or step aside, as a candidate or soldier might, is to retire or pull out.
